notes.substrateHookPoint: INLINE POST-CREATE DRIVE in the composition: deploy/api.ts wraps the REAL execution service with createDeterministicSubstrateExecutions (deploy/preview-substrate.ts) — createExecution delegates to the real service's idempotent create, then (within the substrate worker's own tenant scope) drives the created execution to terminal through the SAME service's own commands, and re-reads the CURRENT durable row so the create response IS the honest terminal receipt. Trade-offs: (+) no background scheduler/queue/worker — the only composition-owned seam that needs none on a serverless isolate; (+) the drive's operations carry deterministic idempotency keys (substrate:<executionId>:<step>), so same-key retries and CONCURRENT drives of the same execution converge on the same durable outcome through the ordinary arbitration; (+) the drive is status-driven and resumable — a retry at any non-terminal state walks only the REMAINING legal edges (pinned by the resume unit test); (+) terminal executions are returned untouched (terminal finality, pinned). (−) the creating request absorbs the drive's round trips (bounded: ~10 governed transactions; the preview plane's executions are exactly the sandbox executions — there is no other runtime behind this plane, stated plainly in PUBLIC-DEPLOYMENT.md §14.3); (−) the drive refuses states it cannot legally walk (WAITING_TOOL/USER/HUMAN, REPLANNING — unreachable on this plane where nothing else drives executions) with the canonical INVALID_STATE_TRANSITION (pinned); (−) the substrateOrigin metadata fact is part of the create fingerprint (a same-key retry of an execution created by an older, unlabeled composition would fail IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED — a one-time upgrade edge, accepted and recorded).
notes.seedingDesign: All seeded identities are DETERMINISTIC functions of the preview application id alone (sha256-derived UUIDs — NO secret material ever enters a durable id, so no offline brute-force oracle exists against the token): the tenant, the application row (the env's id under the deterministic tenant, coherence-verified fail-closed against a foreign owner), the transport principal (external_subject zeck-preview-transport:<appId>) + its OWNER membership, the substrate worker principal + its membership, and the transport credential row (id = credential_id = the deterministic transport-credential id; ACTIVE; label 'Preview transport credential'; role owner; secret_reference zeck-secret://<environment>/transport-token — the material lives ONLY in the deployment environment, never in the record). Every insert is guarded (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING over the schema's unique constraints: PK/unique-slug, the actors' external_subject, the memberships' (actor, application) pair, and the credentials' one-ACTIVE-per-identity partial unique index), so every cold start converges create-if-absent and CONCURRENT isolates arbitrate through the schema itself (pinned: 4 concurrent seedings → one row set). Revocation of the transport credential is TERMINAL — a cold start never resurrects the revoked row (the conflicting insert is skipped and the authenticator honestly reports the revoked status); re-binding after revocation means binding a fresh ZECK_PREVIEW_APPLICATION_ID (the recovery path is documented in PUBLIC-DEPLOYMENT.md §14.2).
notes.materializedVsUnmaterializedShapes: Both pinned by tests/unit/deployment/preview-authorities.test.ts. UNMATERIALIZED (any missing piece of the set): exactly today's honest unbound bootstrap — the identical pinned 26-route table, the honest 401 AUTHENTICATION_FAILED auth boundary (POST /executions probe), the honest 422 CAPABILITY_UNAVAILABLE credential boundary (GET /credentials probe), the truthful composition.authorityMaterialization fact naming the missing variable NAMES ('unmaterialized (ZECK_PG_ADMIN_URL, ZECK_TRANSPORT_TOKEN, ZECK_PREVIEW_APPLICATION_ID absent — exactly the honest unbound bootstrap shape; local/dev behavior unchanged)'). MATERIALIZED: the composition facts report the materialized authority set; the route table is STILL the identical pinned surface; the credentials service is bound with the honest closed issuance gate (issuanceEnabled() === false); and while the cold-start seeding cannot complete (an unreachable relational endpoint, pinned), every bound seam FAILS CLOSED with PROVIDER_ERROR (502) — never a fabricated success. The gate reads ZECK_DATABASE_URL on preview/staging/production and ZECK_PG_ADMIN_URL on local — EXACTLY the variable /health's relational-state probe consumes (mirroring deploy/api.ts's probe), so /health and the materialization gate can never disagree about the relational URL.
notes.asyncColdStartDesign: buildBootstrapApp is synchronous (the hosting adapters — including deploy/vercel.ts, NOT modified by this order — compose it synchronously), so the authorities are CONSTRUCTED synchronously (the pg pool is lazy) and the durable seeding + the baseline policy publication run as the cold-start `ready` promise; the bound authenticate seam awaits the ready gate first, so every credentialed request either sees the completed seed or fails closed (PROVIDER_ERROR with the redacted seeding failure). GET /health independently reports the relational dependency's honest state. The CLI host drains the pool on SIGTERM/SIGINT (BootstrapApp.previewAuthorities.close()); hosted isolates are recycled by the platform instead.
notes.issuanceGateRationale: The DEPLOYED preview composes the platform's environment-materialization secret store (createEnvSecretStore — READ-ONLY by design: 'secrets are stored by the external provisioning plane, never written by the platform') behind createPlatformCredentialSecretStore, so the credential service's DEP-011 issuance gate is honestly CLOSED (issuanceEnabled: false): POST /credentials issue and rotate answer the gate's honest 422 ('credential issuance is not enabled for this deployment...'), GET /credentials is live over SQL and carries issuance.enabled=false, and revoke is live with a REAL effect (the durable row governs the token — pinned on the rail). Opening the gate with the read-only store would either fabricate unresolvable secret references or surface plain 500s; the show-once contract (DEP-011 AC1) cannot be honored against a store that cannot hold the material. The issuance PATH is nonetheless proven end-to-end on the real rail over the SAME SQL authorities with an issuance-capable secret store (issue → the show-once secret authenticates → create → substrate → terminal; rotation retires the predecessor and the successor works) — the exact canonical credentials-world composition. The binding path on the preview is the Lead's directly-materialized journey token (documented in PUBLIC-DEPLOYMENT.md §14.2).
notes.wiringConstraint: The executions/agents/auth public barrels do not export their SQL adapters (createSqlAuthModule, SqlExecutionStore, SqlExecutionsIdempotency, SqlAgentStore); the canonical wiring reference (tests/integration/postgres/executions-world.ts / agents-world.ts / credentials.test.ts) imports the adapter files directly. deploy/preview-authorities.ts mirrors that reference exactly — src/ was never modified. The agents inventory enumeration seam (listAgentIdsOfApplication) is implemented as a read-only SQL query over agents.agents (the AgentStore port exposes no enumeration surface) — the same read-only inventory pattern the api-world and the /health probe use.
notes.policyAdmissionComposition: The execution service's REQUIRED authorize seam is wired to the REAL policy authority (createExecutionAuthorization over createPolicyAuthority with InMemoryPolicyStore + nodePolicyHasher) with a baseline unrestricted set published at cold start (id 'preview-baseline', scope platform, empty selector/restrictions) — the same production composition tests/integration/postgres/agents-world.ts wires ('A baseline permissive set is published so executions authorize (deny-by-default otherwise)'). Without a published set every authorize would deny and no preview execution could run. The honest statement is in PUBLIC-DEPLOYMENT.md §14.1.
